parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime imposes universal, traveler-facing exposures: every trans visitor crosses a national entry system that now issues only birth-sex markers, instructs officers to refuse cases on document doubt and consider a permanent fraud bar, and has produced documented confiscations, stranded travelers and detentions of foreign nationals. The division adds a 2025 facility ban in state buildings and schools, no state gender-identity anti-discrimination or hate-crime coverage, a minor care ban with liability tail, and an arrest precedent with birth-sex holding. Custody harm is documented at national level. No execution or likely-imprisonment pathway exists, courts function and several orders are enjoined, but remedies against the operative exposures are thin. Elevated Risk band, low end.

entry_documents.exposure: National regime restricts passports/visas to birth-sex markers, ended X issuance; officers instructed to refuse on document doubt and weigh permanent fraud ineligibility; documented confiscations, stranded travelers, and detentions of foreign trans nationals; allied governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; limited fraud waivers; litigation pending; legal-aid documentation FAQ.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry screening feeds any later police, hospital or custody encounter; discrepancy can escalate to fraud investigation and detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau adopted conversion-style policies (hair cutting, hormone removal); immigration custody documented forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse; division arrest saw a trans woman handcuffed and held 24 hours in a men's ward; no division custody-placement protection; solitary-confinement compliance prospect raised in debate.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Misdemeanour-level penalty (up to 60 days), release after 24 hours; courts function and several national orders enjoined.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy at entry or in-state can route a visitor into a custody system documented as hostile to trans people.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division 2025 law bans congruent facility use in public schools and state-owned buildings, effective July 2025; national order bars congruent use in federally funded single-sex facilities; trespass criminalisation exists in some states, uncertain here; sports bans apply to visiting athletes.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Trespass-style statutes elsewhere require willful entry plus refusal to leave, with listed exemptions; most other states unmapped bans do not apply here.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Any visit to schools, colleges or state buildings forces birth-sex facility use or ejection/confrontation.

care_services.exposure: Under-18 care banned since 2023 with liability until age 25; national subpoenas of hospital records for under-19 patients; provider liability deters care for travelling minors; religious-refusal statute lets businesses deny services; state terminated an LGBTQ health contract.
care_services.protection: Settlement produced state apology, $300,000 and non-discrimination commitment; national employment-discrimination ruling as backstop.
care_services.interaction: A travelling trans minor cannot continue blockers/hormones here; care-seeking can trigger records exposure for the family.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; DOJ memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; 66-69% public support for birth-sex document and sports rules; state passed no GI protections and allows service refusals.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Memo states powers will not target mere disagreement; reward criteria are violence-related, not identity; pro-trans speech remains lawful and organised.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing raises severity of any outing and licenses social hostility toward visibly trans visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Care ban, provider liability, school 'gender ideology' prosecution directive, sports exclusion, and record-subpoena environment expose a travelling trans minor and guardian; teacher-facilitated transition criminalisation directed nationally.
minors_guardians.protection: Several orders blocked or enjoined; national marriage recognition and employment ruling partly shelter the family unit.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian may face care denial, missed schooling, and inquiry risk; exposure exceeds the adult-alone case.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented trans-specific police action is the bathroom arrest (handcuffing, men's-ward holding); no state hate-crime coverage for gender identity; general violence data not trans-disaggregated here.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; courts reliably process arrests; no documented pattern of street violence against trans visitors in this division.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A visitor reporting hostility relies on national recourse only; local police response is untested beyond the arrest case.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No division anti-discrimination or hate-crime coverage for gender identity; enforcement mechanics of the 2025 facilities law unresolved; whether licence-marker procedures survive the 2026 birth-certificate ruling is unsourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active litigation, functioning national courts, enjoined orders, legal-aid resources; equality protections remain in many other states but not this one.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin state recourse means documented exposures operate without reliable remedy inside this division.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.25-C criminalises cross-dressing in administrative buildings and mandates birth-sex prison housing with frequent assaults. This jurisdiction lacks any presentation-criminal statute, capital exposure is absent, and sentences for the documented trespass arrest were brief. The documented custody brutality here is national-detention-sphere rather than routine local imprisonment. Materially above 0.25-C.

0.35-C's universal lodging-reporting regime produces eviction and fines without imprisonment. This jurisdiction has no equivalent universal in-state reporting, but its entry regime is more punitive than 0.35-C: documented detentions of foreign nationals, potential lifetime fraud bars, and a hostile national custody backdrop. Above 0.35-C on custody severity, but the entry exposure is heavier; net marginally above.

0.45-B features registry-based school verification, nonresident care limited to emergencies, expulsion and weak remedies — closely paralleling this division's minor care ban, facility restrictions in schools and colleges, and absent state remedies. This jurisdiction adds a harsher national entry-document regime and documented custody harms, placing it at or slightly below 0.45-B.

0.55-B involves discretionary secondary screening with refused entry as the worst administrative outcome, written decisions and appeal desks. This jurisdiction's entry regime is more consequential (fraud findings, documented detentions), and it layers a state facility ban, minor care ban, and near-absent state recourse that 0.55-B lacks. Materially below 0.55-B.

0.75-C accepts passports whose markers match presentation, trains officers, provides counsel, compensation and tribunals. For this to be true here, the passport regime would need reversal, the facility ban and minor care ban repeal, and state anti-discrimination and hate-crime coverage in force. All are absent or enjoined-pending, so the case sits far below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is national entry machinery plus a hostile division layered on it. Universal-exposure features dominate: every trans visitor meets the birth-sex passport/visa regime, officer refusal instructions and fraud-bar risk at the border; within the division, state buildings and schools enforce birth-sex facilities, no state remedy exists for discrimination or bias violence, and a travelling minor cannot access care and carries records-subpoena and provider-liability exposure. If outing leads to detention, documented national custody practice (hormone removal, abuse, birth-sex holding) is the operative escalation, not a paper risk. Mitigants are real but partial: courts enjoin several measures, penalties documented so far are misdemeanour-level, national hate-crime and employment protections exist, and no imprisonment-likely or capital pathway is documented. The worst tier-1 exposures (facility exclusion, entry document regime) with thin working recourse place this in the Elevated band near its lower edge; a family with a trans minor faces the heavier end of the same rating.
